Challenges

Sound familiar?

“Guest post offers land in our inbox daily — and they’re all junk.”

That market sells placements on content farms. We work the other end: real publications with editors, audiences and standards.

“Our experts have no time to write articles.”

They don’t have to. We draft from interviews and their positions; they approve the final piece — an hour of their time, not a week.

“Editors keep rejecting our pitches.”

Pitches fail when they read like ads. Ours lead with an angle the editor’s readers gain from, matched to the publication’s style.

“We got published, but nobody read it.”

Placement quality is the whole game: we target publications your buyers actually read, and report referral traffic alongside links.

“Our bylines make claims legal would never approve.”

Articles are drafted from your experts’ approved positions and pass your review before submission — nothing publishes unapproved.

“Guest posts didn’t move our rankings.”

A handful of strong, relevant placements beats dozens of weak ones. Targets are chosen for topical relevance to the pages you need to rank.

“Agencies won’t tell us where posts will run.”

The target list is agreed with you before pitching starts — you approve every publication in advance.

“It all feels like buying links with extra steps.”

The difference is editorial reality: an editor chose the piece because readers benefit. That is exactly what search engines reward.

FAQs

FAQs on guest posting services

How many posts per month?

Programs are built around quality targets — typically a handful of strong placements beats dozens of weak ones. Your plan sets the cadence.

Can we approve articles and sites?

Yes — both the target list and every article are approved by you before anything is pitched or published.

Are these sites relevant to our industry?

Relevance is the first filter; a smaller in-niche publication beats a big unrelated one.

Do you write under our names?

Yes — ghost-written under your experts' bylines, from their positions, with their approval.

Do we approve articles before they are submitted?

Always. Drafts are written from your experts’ positions, reviewed by your team, and only submitted once you sign off.
